text:
incident-bot: [PAGER P1] BlueHorizon (customer: bluehorizon-prod) — private VPC vpc-0a1b2c reporting widespread 503s at the NLB -> ALB path. Pager fired 2026-03-15 04:12 UTC. Impact: customer inference traffic failing; elevated error rate. Incident link: https://redwood/incident/INC-330123

Nina (oncall): on it. I’m ssh-ing into the tenant NAT proxies and checking NLB target health. tagging @Kai M for ALB health checks and @Maya Ops for DNS/route checks.

Kai M: seeing ALB -> backend 502/connection refused in ALB logs. NLB target group shows many targets Unhealthy with reason="connection-refused". healthcheck path /healthz returns ECONNREFUSED.

Maya Ops: DNS A record for bluehorizon.app points to nlb-1111.elb (public ip). TTL 30s. No recent DNS changes in last 24h. Status page updated (partial outage). status-bot: status page updated: "BlueHorizon: degraded - inference API returns 503 from private deployment" :warning:

Leon SRE: checking conntrack and NAT metrics on tenant proxies: conntrack count at 98% of conntrack-limit, spikes align with error window. suspect NAT exhaustion causing upstream connection resets. 

Nina (oncall): that matches: internal healthchecks from ALB -> backend are TCP; if conntrack is exhausted backend rejects -> connection refused. quick mitigation: increase conntrack on proxies and add a temporary SG rule to allow healthcheck probes to bypass NAT? need approval.

Kai M: confirming target group health details via AWS:
```bash
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456:targetgroup/tg-bluehorizon/abcd1234 
```
sample output: 
```json
{ "TargetHealthDescriptions": [ { "Target": { "Id": "10.0.5.12", "Port": 8080 }, "HealthCheckPort": "8080", "TargetHealth": { "State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "ConnectionRefused" } } ] }
```

Maya Ops: customer-side CNAME was fine. TTL low so we can shift weight quickly. We have a warm standby (dedicated pool) in eu-west-1 that can handle traffic; we can fail traffic there while we fix tenant NAT. Suggest: 1) apply temporary SG egress rule for model subnet 2) shift DNS weight to standby 3) increase conntrack on proxies.

Nina (oncall): steps I will perform now (in order):
1) Add temporary outbound SG rule to tenant-proxy-sg allowing 10.0.0.0/16:443,8080 -> command:
```bash
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0proxy --protocol tcp --port 8080 --cidr 10.0.0.0/16
```
2) Increase conntrack limits on proxies: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` then persist via SSM runbook.
3) Drain unhealthy targets from NLB TG and register warm backends.

Leon SRE: +1 for SG change and conntrack bump. Note: SG change must be scoped to model subnet (10.0.0.0/16) not 0.0.0.0/0. I’ll prepare the SSM document to roll conntrack across the fleet.

Maya Ops: initiating DNS weight shift to standby 20% now to reduce pressure while we remediate. I’ll monitor error rate and answer any customer queries.

Sam K: I’m taking the hands-on for the SG change. Nina, you want me to run the authorize command?

Nina (oncall): yes, please. run it and post the command output. Also keep an eye on healthcheck metrics. If traffic improves, we can slowly shift weight back.

Sam K: running now...
```bash
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0proxy --protocol tcp --port 8080 --cidr 10.0.0.0/16
{ "Return": true }
```
Sam K: SG change applied.

Leon SRE: conntrack bump applied on two proxy hosts via SSM runbook, propagation starting. conntrack usage falling from 98% -> 60% on first hosts.

Kai M: re-checking target status... target health transitioning to healthy for 3/5 hosts. ALB 5xx rate dropping.

Maya Ops: DNS shift to standby increased to 50% to reduce risk while we watch. status-bot: status page updated: "BlueHorizon: partial degradation, traffic shifted to standby" :information_source:

Nina (oncall): traffic is restoring. keep monitoring for 30m. I’ll prepare a short customer update: we identified NAT/conntrack saturation plus a restrictive egress SG preventing ALB healthchecks; applied targeted SG egress rule and increased conntrack; shifted traffic to standby until full recovery.

Sam K: I’ll continue on-call for the next 4h (handoff). Nina, please add any follow-ups to INC-330123: postmortem, guardrail to prevent future conntrack exhaustion, revert SG change once stable.

Nina (oncall): confirmed handoff to @Sam K at 04:42 UTC. Thanks team.

status-bot: incident updated -> RESOLVED (mitigated) at 04:58 UTC. Final notes: targeted SG egress applied, conntrack limits increased (temporary), DNS weighted failover used. Action items: permanent conntrack tuning + autoscaling, tighter monitoring alerts, postmortem.

Sam K: leaving final note in ticket: impact window 04:12-04:58 UTC, customer traffic restored, follow-ups queued.

Nina (oncall): closing thread here, will add a short blameless postmortem. :thumbsup:
